assessment_summary:
I reviewed the guide and the installation summary, then independently inspected the environment rather than relying on the summary. The install used the source-build path (npm install + vite build) rather than the guide's prebuilt Bitbucket examples.zip; the guide notes the resulting layout (Basic/mastercode folders with config.js/config.json/index.html, resources/, js/masterportal.js, css/masterportal.css, img, locales). The produced /workspace/dist matches that layout: three example portals (basic/master/auto) each with config and resources, plus a versioned mastercode folder containing the compiled bundle, CSS, logo/draw SVGs, and 11 locale sets.

I validated behavior, not just file existence: I served the built output over HTTP and confirmed the entry HTML, JS bundle, CSS, config files, and resources all return 200 with correct sizes; I confirmed the bundle is syntactically valid; I confirmed all config JSON parses; I started the documented Vite dev server and confirmed it serves a portal whose module graph resolves and transforms correctly; and I ran a portion of the project's own test suite (4/4 passing). These together demonstrate the software is installed, complete, and operational.

The only unverified aspect is full in-browser rendering, because no browser or headless browser is installed. My jsdom attempt to execute the production bundle hung during startup, which is a known limitation of that non-browser environment for this WebGL/i18n-heavy app and is explicitly not counted as failure per the validation rules. No prohibited actions were taken; I did not install, build, edit, or repair anything, and all temporary servers I started were stopped.
